newsitem.title: USA: Albright to visit Balkans later in May.
newsitem.headline: Albright to visit Balkans later in May.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, placing new emphasis on peace efforts in Bosnia, will visit Sarajevo the weekend of May 31 and may also visit other venues in the Balkans, the U.S. State Department said on Tuesday.
"There is a lot of concern" that parties to the U.S.-mediated Bosnia peace agreement are "falling down" on their commitments, spokesman Nicholas Burns said in announcing Albright's travel plans.

Burns said Albright would travel to Paris on Sunday, where she planned to meet officials from France and other countries on Monday ahead of Tuesday's signing of the new Russia-NATO partnership agreement.

She joins U.S. President Bill Clinton in the Hague for the U.S.-European Union summit, then flies on Wednesday night to Sintra, Portugal for a semi-annual NATO foreign ministers meeting that will focus on alliance expansion plans. There will also be a meeting of foreign ministers from countries involved in implementing the Bosnia peace deal.

Burns said Albright's schedule was not yet set but she planned to visit Sarajevo the weekend of May 31 for talks with Bosnian President Alija Izetbegovic. She also is "considering a range of other options for travel to other places in the Balkans" and will visit U.S. troops in the region, he said.

Albright aims to press Bosnia's three rival ethnic groups -- Serbs, Croats and Moslems -- as well as Croatia and Serbia to implement the Bosnia peace agreement, including on issues such as bringing war criminals to justice and allowing displaced persons to return to their homes, he said.
